scenarios.input: Transcribe a synthetic two-speaker WAV with labels.
scenarios.expected: Return the transcript ID, selected speaker labels and timestamps, and any unprocessed span.
evidence: Resolve the supported API fields, submit the authorized asset once, then poll the same transcript ID to a terminal status.
Return the transcript ID, selected speaker labels and timestamps, and any unprocessed span.

scenarios.input: The audio URL is private and processing consent is missing.
scenarios.expected: If the asset is ambiguous, private without consent, or the status is unknown, stop before resubmitting. Terminate streaming sessions you opened.
evidence: Identify the exact audio source, consent to process it, and whether speaker labels, redaction or streaming are required.
If the asset is ambiguous, private without consent, or the status is unknown, stop before resubmitting. Terminate streaming sessions you opened.
Never swap in a look-alike or stock voice silently.
send it only after that speaker said yes in the current task.

scenarios.input: An ABACare narration companion is attached and the approved script is ready.
scenarios.expected: Check connection state, verify the configured voice without generating, use the accepted take, and report the real job, WAV, captions and what remains unfinished.
evidence: Check the voice connection state first. A cached check or saved default is not current availability.

A live check that opens a TTS WebSocket, reads `Begin` and sends no `Generate` proves acceptance of the configured voice only. It does not prove private visibility, upload source, consent attestation or speaker identity; those stay separate evidence.
Reuse binds the caller, the exact approved script, the saved voice and any take label. Do not change punctuation, title or label to force a fresh paid take.
On timeout, an unknown status or a lost response, recover the original job id instead of creating a new one: the provider may already have finished and billed it.
Take captions and word timings from the same accepted WAV, by alignment or transcription if the generator returned none. Never resynthesize the script to obtain captions.
A completed WAV is not a finished reel. Keep the approved source media, inspect pronunciation, pacing and synchronization, review the encoded video, and report actual artifacts and status.
